questions.q: Where did Amr bin Luhay bring the idol Hubal back from?
questions.explain: Amr bin Luhay saw the people of Sham worshipping idols and wanted to bring one home.
Masjid comes from the word sujud, so it is a place of prostration.

questions.q: We face the Kaaba when praying. Whom do we worship?
questions.explain: The Kaaba is the qiblah, not what is worshipped. We worship Allah alone.

questions.q: What was the name of the first great idol set before the Kaaba?
questions.explain: Hubal was the first great idol at the Kaaba, brought by Amr bin Luhay.

questions.q: Which new idols were made after Hubal?
questions.explain: Distant tribes took home new idols such as Lat, Uzza and Manat.

questions.q: The five idols the ustaz mentioned come from the time of which prophet?
questions.explain: Five righteous men of the time of Prophet Nuh eventually became idols that were worshipped.

questions.q: How did statues of righteous men end up being worshipped?
options: They were made to remember them, then over time were worshipped
They were made by a king to frighten the people
They were built by Prophet Ibrahim
questions.explain: Statues meant to remember the righteous ended up being worshipped. Exalting the righteous excessively is dangerous.

questions.q: Prophet Ibrahim built the Kaaba without idols.
questions.explain: True. He called people to worship Allah alone.

questions.q: Idols spread through tribes who came for Hajj and took new idols home.
questions.explain: True. Idols spread through the pilgrimage when distant tribes took them home.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Amr bin Luhay goes to Sham
The Prophet SAW reflects in the Cave of Hira
Hubal is placed at the Kaaba

questions.explain: Amr bin Luhay went to Sham, Hubal was set up, idols spread, and in that darkness the Prophet SAW reflected in the Cave of Hira.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: The direction of the Kaaba faced in prayer
The first great idol at the Kaaba

questions.explain: A masjid is a place of prostration, the qiblah is the direction of the Kaaba, Hubal was the first idol, and ummi means unable to read and write.

questions.q: What etiquette for entering the mosque did the ustaz mention?
options: Enter with the right foot and recite the supplication
questions.explain: Enter with the right foot and recite the supplication so that Allah opens the doors of mercy.
